title: Segmented network-posture intake and staged OS/firmware upgrade lanes for private deployments
creator: Mei Chen
description:
Background:

We are seeing repeated customer asks that fall between 'simple VPC' and 'fully air-gapped' categories: examples include isolated VLANs with restricted egress via proxy, datacenters that only allow scheduled OS/firmware windows, and customers who require staged patching with rollback guarantees. Current intake funnels conflate these signals which leads to under-scoped engagements and delayed schedules.

Goal:
Define a lightweight, repeatable intake flow and prioritization rubric that: (1) classifies customer network posture into actionable lanes (Open VPC / Proxy-limited / Isolated VLAN / Air-gapped), (2) ties each lane to a minimum viable upgrade/runbook profile (eg. required maintenance window cadence, preferred transport mechanisms, supported patch strategy), and (3) surfaces clear decision points for sales/solutions to commit to SLAs or escalation.

Scope and deliverables:
- Draft a segmented network-posture taxonomy and one-page intake form for solutions engineering.
- Create 3 staged upgrade lanes (Rapid: 48–72h; Scheduled: 1–4 weeks; Sequenced: >4 weeks with staged rollouts & operator assistance).
- Define per-lane checklist: preflight tests, allowed transport (S3 proxy, USB media, internal registry), rollback criteria, telemetry required for post-upgrade verification.
- Add gating logic to intake UI so requests auto-route to proper fastlane/concierge queue.
- Provide a short customer-facing expectations doc and internal playbook for engagement handoff.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Intake form prototypes exist in Confluence and link in this ticket.
2) Taxonomy maps to concrete technical checks (connectivity probes, allowed egress endpoints) and a sample preflight script for SRE/SE.
3) Prioritization rubric scores requests deterministically and maps to an assigned lane.
4) A single PR (or small set) updates the Console intake UI wiring to include the new fields (backend stub acceptable for phase 1).
5) Two pilot customers (one proxy-limited, one isolated VLAN) are signed up for a staged rollout using the new lane definitions.

Trade-offs and discussion items:
- Conservative lane definitions reduce surprises but increase manual work in the short term. We propose a phased rollout: start with manual review for Sequenced lane, then automate rules for Rapid/Scheduled.
- We must avoid over-committing SLAs for Sequenced lane; recommend offering a "concierge" paid assistance package.
- Security review required for any lane that permits external media or operator-assisted upgrades (security_review_required=true).

Implementation notes:
- Work with Runtime/Infra to identify the minimal telemetry hooks we can require without leaking customer-sensitive payloads (token-level telemetry is NOT allowed).
- Create preflight probes: TCP connect to pinned endpoints, DNS resolution checks, time-window verification. Script template: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy-playbooks/blob/main/preflight/probe-template.sh
- Console changes: add dropdown for "Network Posture" and "Preferred Upgrade Cadence". Back-end property: "customer_posture" string. Phase 1 can use an Admin-only form.

Stakeholders and reviewers:
- Solutions Eng: Priya Nair (review intake UX)
- Security: Daniel Ortiz (security gating)
- Runtime/Infra: Jordan Blake (telemetry & preflight probes)
- Sales/Customer Success: Laila Gomez (customer comms & pilot coordination)

Pilot customers (identified):
- Acme Health (proxy-limited, requires scheduled OS windows)
- QuantumBank (isolated VLAN, requires sequenced rollout and signed rollback plan)

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: Underestimating customer network constraints leading to failed upgrades. Mitigation: Require at least one successful preflight for Sequenced lane before any scheduled upgrade date.
- Risk: Escalation volume for Sequenced lane. Mitigation: Offer paid concierge and cap SLA commitments in product docs.

Next steps (initial sprint):
- Week 0: Draft taxonomy + intake form (owner: Mei Chen).
- Week 1: Align with Security & Runtime on preflight scripts (owner: Ethan Patel).
- Week 2: Wire Admin-only intake in Console + pilot run with Acme Health (owner: Solutions Eng).

Notes on communication: Attach final intake form to new customer onboarding email and the Partner Portal. Include a short checklist in the Solutions Eng kickoff template.
